question: The resumed meeting of the parties to the COP16 Global Biodiversity Conference (GCB) concluded with an agreement on subjects ranging from the Strategy for Resource Mobilisation to improving the monitoring of the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) and determining how the indicators should be measured and used and how progress on the implementation of the GBF should be reviewed at COP17. 1.

Given that just over 17 % of the signatories to the Convention on Biological Diversity have submitted their action plans to protect biodiversity, how does the Commission assess the outcome of the resumed meeting, and how should the above figure influence the mobilisation of resources from which instruments, mechanisms and institutions should effectively benefit?

How will the financial pledges made at COP16 influence the way in which the Commission determines how resources are mobilised and subsidies harmful to nature are redirected as part of the EU’s budget and policies?

Seeing that a number of countries have, according to certain studies, made weak pledges to protect the environment, what will the Commission do to improve how indicators are monitored, used and measured and how the implementation of the GBF is reviewed?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2025) The resumed session of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) Conference of the Parties (COP)16 agreed on the crucial issues of resource mobilisation, technical updates to the monitoring framework and procedures for the global review of implementation at COP17 and 19.

This allows CBD processes to continue and provides wider impetus for multilateral environmental negotiations. 48 Parties submitted revised national biodiversity strategies and action plans whilst 125 Parties uploaded national targets aligned with the Kunming Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF). There is ongoing work in other Parties. Parties also implement the GBF through other policies.

The seventh national reports to be submitted by all Parties by February 2026 will allow a more complete analysis. A further increase of resources from all sources will be necessary for achieving target 19 of the GBF. The Commission and Member States will continue work in this regard, leveraging private finance and public budgets – including through the multiannual financial framework1.

The identification, phasing out or repurposing of harmful subsidies remains extremely important. The Commission is implementing the updated GBF monitoring framework at EU level. This will continue in the years to come and will support the assessment of progress in implementation of the GBF in the seventh and eighth national reports to the CBD, which are due in 2026 and 2029, respectively.

The Commission is consulting the Member States on the use of indicators in view of increasing synergies in the reporting exercise, facilitating this work, maximising coherence and minimising duplication of efforts. CBD COP17 will review the use of indicators at the global level.
